title: Vermeer
objective: After this level you can describe Vermeer's quiet interiors and how he painted light.
summary: Only about 36 Vermeers survive. In The Milkmaid, window light falls on a still kitchen, built from hundreds of colored dots. Whether he used a camera obscura is still debated.

cards.headline: Only about 36 paintings by Vermeer survive.
cards.body: He worked in Delft, and outside his region he was little known until the 1800s, when the critic Théophile Thoré brought him international fame. So what makes so few quiet pictures so famous? Mostly one thing: the light.

cards.headline: The loudest thing is the milk
cards.body: In The Milkmaid (about 1660), a maid stands at a table and pours milk from a jug into a bowl. Bread sits beside her. Daylight falls through a window on the left and fills the small kitchen. Except for the thin stream of milk, everything is still. No drama, no saints, no crowd. Just someone doing a chore, and doing it with total care.

cards.fact: Vermeer built light out of dots.
cards.context: Look closely at The Milkmaid and the light on the bread and the jug breaks into hundreds of small colored dots of paint. Some are blurred little spots, like the sparkle in an out-of-focus photo. Step back and they turn into crust catching the sun.

cards.headline: Did he use a camera?
cards.body: Those blurred light spots match what you see in a camera obscura, a device that projects an image through a lens. So some think Vermeer used one. But no document from his time shows he owned or used a camera obscura. It stays a debated idea, a good guess with no receipt.

cards.headline: Vermeer: quiet light
learned: The Milkmaid: window light, stillness, a stream of milk
